name: Performance bonus
description: The entry quantity is the performance bonus for the period; it is additional wages. Practical treatment: SSS/MPF/EC and HDMF use ordinary wages; PHIC uses basic salary; 13th month and Christmas bonus are outside all four monthly bases. The SSS IRR expressly excludes Christmas bonus and does not name 13th month. WTAX uses final gross and includes both in the 90,000 aggregate benefits pool. If a written SSS ruling requires 13th-month inclusion, change only the SSS checkpoint routing.

references.title: Labor Code art.100; company policy or CBA: a performance bonus is a contractual benefit, not a statutory wage.

name: Christmas bonus
description: The entry quantity is the separately promised Christmas bonus for the period; it is additional wages, never the de minimis Christmas gift. Practical treatment: SSS/MPF/EC and HDMF use ordinary wages; PHIC uses basic salary; 13th month and Christmas bonus are outside all four monthly bases. The SSS IRR expressly excludes Christmas bonus and does not name 13th month. WTAX uses final gross and includes both in the 90,000 aggregate benefits pool. If a written SSS ruling requires 13th-month inclusion, change only the SSS checkpoint routing.

references.title: Labor Code art.100; company policy or CBA: a Christmas bonus promised separately from the statutory 13th-month pay is a contractual benefit. SSS IRR (2019) Rule 12 s.6(iii) excludes a Christmas bonus from the monthly salary credit; NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e) and RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(11) include it in the PHP90,000 aggregate benefits pool.

name: Back pay – basic

references.title: 13th-month basic includes eligible basic salary differentials and maternity salary differential. Required earning_year attributes this actual amount to its earned calendar year independently of cash payment year; split cross-year amounts. classification_reference identifies the underlying wage/leave adjustment evidence.

name: Back pay – duty allowance

references.title: Labor Code art.100; RA 6727 wage orders: an unpaid contractual allowance owed for past periods is back pay.

name: Back pay – additional wages

references.title: Labor Code art.100; RA 6727 wage orders: an unpaid wage adjustment owed for past periods is back pay.

name: Commission

references.title: SSS/Pag-IBIG remuneration and WTAX supplementary compensation unchanged.13th-month treatment is factual: direct personal-sales commissions forming salary are included (Philippine Duplicators); productivity/profit-sharing/overriding commissions are excluded unless integrated into basic by agreement/practice. Required commission_basis and classification_reference preserve that genuine classification; a blanket commission exclusion is incorrect. Reyes vNLRC,GR160233,8August2007.

name: 13th month pay
description: The entry quantity is the 13th-month amount due for the entitlement year; the engine posts it as gross earnings. Practical treatment: SSS/MPF/EC and HDMF use ordinary wages; PHIC uses basic salary; 13th month and Christmas bonus are outside all four monthly bases. The SSS IRR expressly excludes Christmas bonus and does not name 13th month. WTAX uses final gross and includes both in the 90,000 aggregate benefits pool. If a written SSS ruling requires 13th-month inclusion, change only the SSS checkpoint routing.

references.title: PD851/DOLE2024 Handbook ch.13 C-H; Reyes GR160233; PAL GR142399. Automatic calculation uses original payroll_history and ordered current.priced_lines: signed eligible basic by earning_year, documented personal-sales/integrated components, less actual13th/evidenced equivalent grants only for matching entitlement_year. Current component dependencies order maternity/basic-backpay/commission and other selected awards before13th regardless input order. HR supplies dated source-completeness and confirmed attendance/salary-through facts, not a calculated total. Year-end daily additional unpriced paid days multiply an unchanged captured daily rate. Future unknown records, missing original attribution/classification or unsupported rate changes require the existing dated reviewed residual-base fallback or refuse. A later change requires a differential. Generic gifts and separately promised CBA Christmas bonuses never become automatic credits.

name: Separation pay
description: The entry quantity is the separation amount; the recorded termination cause and service remain the legal basis.

references.title: Labor Code art.298: one month’s pay or one month per year of service, whichever is higher, on termination for installation of labour-saving devices or redundancy; art.298–299: half a month per year or one month, whichever is higher, on retrenchment, closure not due to serious losses, or disease. A fraction of at least six months counts as a year. Labor Code arts.298–299: one month’s pay per year of service (redundancy, the only authorised cause the exit reasons distinguish; a fraction of at least six months counts as a year), never less than one month. Tax: exempt under NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b) as pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control (redundancy or retrenchment), so the class counts toward nothing and no withholding scheme reads it. the exit fact `termination_cause` chooses the award — labour-saving devices or redundancy one month a year (art.298); retrenchment, a closure not due to serious losses, or disease half a month a year (arts.298–299); a closure due to serious business losses owes none (art.298: the half-month award is for closures "not due to serious business losses"). a termination for disease recorded as a dismissal or unilateral termination of a non-domestic employee (exit fact `terminated_for_disease`) pays the same one month or half a month per year, whichever is greater (Labor Code art.299, formerly art.284; E-Library PD 442 text art.323: "at least to one (1) month salary or to one-half (1/2) month salary for every year of service, whichever is greater"); tax-exempt as separation for sickness (NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b)). A kasambahay's disease is a just cause under RA 10361 s.34(f) with no separation pay. Years of service are `round(service_months / 12, 1, HALF_UP)`: a fraction of at least six months counts as a year (corrected in every version from a tenth-of-a-year rounding); the month’s pay is the contract’s monthly wage, basic plus fixed allowances (`terms.monthly_wage`). Causes are the exit fact `termination_cause` (customer input), incl. a security guard or contractor’s worker without assignment (half a month a year) and an impossible reinstatement (a month a year), DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.14 §C. A bona fide suspension of operations beyond six months (Labor Code art.301; Omnibus Rules Book VI Rule I s.12 as amended by DOLE DO 215-20, https://web.archive.org/web/2021id_/https://www.dole.gov.ph/php_assets/uploads/2020/10/DO-215-20-Rule-Amending-Section-12-of-Rule-I-Rules-Implementing-Book-VI-of-the-Labor-Code-on-Suspension-of-Employment-Relationship.pdf, read 2026-10-07: the relationship is suspended for not more than six months, extendable by six in a declared national emergency; an employee retrenched before or after the extension is "entitled to separation pay as prescribed by the Labor Code", and "the first six (6) months of suspension of employment shall be included in the computation") is the cause `SUSPENSION_OVER_SIX_MONTHS`: the retrenchment award, half a month a year, at least a month, the suspension months counting as service.

name: Protection-order support (RA 9262)

references.title: RA 9262 s.8(g): a protection order may direct the respondent to provide support, and notwithstanding other laws to the contrary the court orders an appropriate percentage of the respondent's income or salary withheld regularly by the employer and automatically remitted directly to the woman; failure to withhold or remit, or delay without justifiable cause, makes the employer liable for indirect contempt. Added in place 2026-09-29 in every version (ML-2, a transcription omission: RA 9262 predates every version). The percentage is the court's, so the employer deducts exactly the amount the served order fixes for the period, entered by HR with the order as evidence. Owner rule 2026-09-28: the Act is silent on how the employer books the withholding; default a net-pay deduction after every statutory line, touching no SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG or withholding base, because the support is paid out of the respondent's own compensation. Remittance to the payee is an external payment (obligation PROTECTION_ORDER_SUPPORT_WITHHOLDING).

name: Retirement pay
description: The entry quantity is the RA 7641 retirement amount; age, service and establishment exemptions gate the definition. A retirement plan does not: where it pays less than RA 7641, this class pays the difference (DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.15 §E).

references.title: RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302): an employee retiring at 60 to 65 after at least five years’ service, with no retirement plan, is paid half a month’s salary for every year of service — 22.5 days: fifteen days, the five-day service incentive leave and one twelfth of the 13th-month pay — a fraction of at least six months counting as a year. RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302): optional retirement from sixty and compulsory at sixty-five, after five years’ service — a person retiring past sixty-five is inside it; retail, service and agricultural establishments of not more than ten workers are outside (`company.facts.small_establishment`). One-half month salary is 22.5 days of the daily rate, the daily rate being the monthly basic on the person’s own factor (365 for the monthly-paid, 313 on a six-day week, 261 on five). Tax: the statutory benefit is exempt under NIRC s.32(B)(6)(a), which is why this class pays the RA 7641 minimum only — any excess over it under a company plan would be tested against RA 4917 (age 50, ten years’ service, BIR-qualified plan). the exemption is its own required entity fact, `company.facts.retirement_exempt_establishment` — RA 7641 exempts retail, service and agricultural establishments of not more than ten employees, a different class from the SIL exemption of any establishment regularly employing fewer than ten (`small_establishment`); a small manufacturer owes retirement pay. The daily rate is the monthly basic × 12 ÷ the contract term fact `days_per_year` (313 when unrecorded); the exemption is the entity fact `retirement_exempt_establishment`. Handbook ch.15 §B: retirement "upon reaching the age of 60 years or more but not beyond 65 years". RA 8558 and RA 10757: an underground or surface mine worker (contract-term fact `mine_worker`, customer input) retires from fifty, compulsorily at sixty, after five years as a mine worker. Past the compulsory age: sixty-five (sixty for a mine worker) makes retirement compulsory; it does not forfeit the RA 7641 benefit, so an employee kept on and retired later is paid it.

name: Uniform and clothing allowance

references.title: RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 11-2018 (and RR 4-2025 for uniforms and achievement awards, from 30 January 2025) (e): uniform and clothing allowance to ₱7,000 a year: a de minimis benefit, outside compensation to the ceiling; the excess is an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e)) — the DE_MINIMIS_UNIFORM checkpoint, capped over the calendar year.

references.title: RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 11-2018 (and RR 4-2025 for uniforms and achievement awards, from 30 January 2025) (i): Christmas and major anniversary gifts to ₱5,000 a year: a de minimis benefit, outside compensation to the ceiling; the excess is an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e)) — the DE_MINIMIS_GIFT checkpoint, capped over the calendar year.

name: CBA and productivity incentive benefit

references.title: RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 11-2018 (and RR 4-2025 for uniforms and achievement awards, from 30 January 2025) (k): benefits under a CBA and a productivity incentive scheme, combined, to ₱10,000 a year: a de minimis benefit, outside compensation to the ceiling; the excess is an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e)) — the DE_MINIMIS_CBA checkpoint, capped over the calendar year.

name: Overtime or night-shift meal allowance

references.title: RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 11-2018 (and RR 4-2025 for uniforms and achievement awards, from 30 January 2025) (j): a daily meal allowance for overtime work or a night/graveyard shift is de minimis to 25% of the region’s basic minimum wage for each such day (the region’s monthly figure × 12 ÷ 313 is the daily wage the order states). The ceiling bounds the exemption, never the pay: the class pays what the employer keyed, whole. the DE_MINIMIS_OT_MEAL checkpoint is exempt to 25% × the daily minimum wage × the days (the run’s dates with overtime or night-window hours); the excess is an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph; RMC 50-2018: “benefits given in excess of the maximum amount allowed as de minimis benefits shall be included as part of ‘other benefits’”).

name: Kasambahay unjustified-departure salary forfeiture
description: The entry quantity is the unpaid salary; the deduction is capped at fifteen days at the recorded daily rate.

references.title: RA 10361 s.32: a domestic worker who leaves without justifiable reason forfeits unpaid salary of no more than fifteen days. This NET deduction is capped by the final payslip’s unpaid salary; the thirteenth-month pay and leave conversion are not salary for this cap. The day is the monthly wage × 12 ÷ the contract term fact `days_per_year` (313 when unrecorded). The entry amount is the unpaid salary; at most fifteen days of it is forfeited.

name: Kasambahay unjust-dismissal indemnity
description: The entry quantity records the indemnity; the amount is fifteen days at the recorded daily rate.

references.title: RA 10361 s.32: "If the domestic worker is unjustly dismissed, the domestic worker shall be paid the compensation already earned plus the equivalent of fifteen (15) days work by way of indemnity". The Act is silent on the day: fifteen of the version’s ordinary days (`terms.ordinary_day`, the monthly basic over `ordinary_divisor_days`), the day every other PH day-rate reads. Tax: a separation for a cause beyond the employee’s control, NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b), so the class counts toward nothing, like SEPARATION_PAY. The pay-request person context evaluates the version’s ordinary divisor and roster week on the event date. The day is the monthly wage × 12 ÷ the contract term fact `days_per_year` (313 when unrecorded).

name: Maternity salary differential
description: The entry quantity is the full salary for the leave less the SSS maternity benefit.

references.title: RA 11210 s.5(c) and its IRR Rule VI: the employer pays the difference between the full salary and the SSS maternity benefit, unless exempt — a distressed establishment, a retail or service establishment of ten or fewer, a micro business, or one already paying the equivalent (entity fact `maternity_differential_exempt`, customer input). Customer input: `entry.amount`, the full salary for the leave less the SSS benefit. Exempt from withholding (RMC 105-2019: payments of benefits under the SSS law, RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(B)(1)(e)), so it counts toward no scheme.

13th-month basic includes eligible basic salary differentials and maternity salary differential. Required earning_year attributes this actual amount to its earned calendar year independently of cash payment year; split cross-year amounts. classification_reference identifies the underlying wage/leave adjustment evidence.

name: Hazard pay

references.title: NIRC s.24(A)(2); RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(13): hazard pay is compensation (SSS, Pag-IBIG) that a minimum wage earner receives exempt (the STATUTORY_WAGES checkpoint). Customer input: the amount the employer’s hazard-pay plan pays.

name: Service charge share

references.title: Labor Code art.96 as amended by RA 11360 s.1: service charges collected by hotels, restaurants and similar establishments are distributed completely and equally among the covered workers, managerial employees excepted; they are not counted toward the minimum wage. Customer input: the employee’s equal share of the period’s collections. Compensation for SSS, Pag-IBIG and WTAX.

name: Union dues and agency fees

references.title: Labor Code art.113(b) and the check-off provisions (arts.250(o), 259(e) as renumbered): deducted only with the employee’s written authorisation (`evidence` REQUIRED); NIRC s.32(B)(7)(f) and RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(B)(12): excluded from taxable compensation (the UNION_DUES checkpoint, which WTAX subtracts).

name: Pag-IBIG voluntary contribution

references.title: RA 9679 s.7: an employee may elect to contribute above the mandatory share; only the mandatory employee share is excluded from compensation (NIRC s.32(B)(7)(f)), so the voluntary amount is deducted after tax. Customer input: the elected amount (`evidence` REQUIRED).

name: Pag-IBIG MP2 savings

references.title: RA 9679 s.7; Pag-IBIG MP2 programme: a voluntary savings deduction on the employee’s election, after tax. Customer input: the elected amount (`evidence` REQUIRED).

name: Deduction for loss or damage
description: The entry quantity is the assessed loss; the deduction is capped at 20% of the period's basic pay.

references.title: Labor Code arts.113–114; Omnibus Rules Implementing the Labor Code Book III Rule VIII s.14: a deduction for loss or damage to the employer’s tools, materials or equipment only where the employee is clearly responsible and was heard (`evidence` REQUIRED), never above the actual loss and "not exceed 20 percent of the employee’s wages in a week" — capped at 20% of the period’s basic. A kasambahay is never charged for loss or damage (RA 10361 s.14). In a month paid at two frequencies (`period.switched`) the period’s basic is the slip’s settled share: the month from `period.month_from` to `period.to` less the earlier slips. Recorded default (weekly cap): Rule VIII s.14(c) limits the deduction to "20 percent of the employee’s wages in a week"; a deduction made on a pay day is read as spread over the period’s weeks, so the cap is 20% of the period’s basic — the sum of 20% of each of its weeks’ wages. An entry above the cap is cut to it (`on_exceed: CAP`); HR enters any remainder in a later period.

name: Fringe benefit (in kind)
description: The entry quantity is the monetary value of the benefit in kind; it is employer cost only.

references.title: NIRC s.33; RR 11-2018 s.2.33: a benefit in kind (housing, vehicle, membership, …) is priced and settled but adds no pay: for supervisory and managerial staff it is the FBT scheme’s base, for rank-and-file it is taxable compensation (WTAX adds the FRINGE_BENEFIT checkpoint). Customer input: the monetary value under RR 3-98 s.2.33(B).

name: Separation pay (taxable)

references.title: NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b): only separation pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control (death, sickness, disability, an authorised cause) is excluded; a payment on resignation or under a company plan for any other cause is taxable compensation. Customer input: the amount.

name: Retirement pay (taxable)

references.title: NIRC s.32(B)(6)(a): retirement benefits under RA 7641, or under a reasonable private plan to an employee of at least fifty with ten years’ service, availed once, are excluded; any other retirement payment is taxable compensation. Customer input: the amount.

name: SSS sickness benefit (advanced)
description: The entry quantity is the SSS-computed sickness benefit advanced by the employer.

references.title: RA 11199 s.14: the employer pays a confined member 90% of the average daily salary credit for each compensable day from the fourth, at most 120 days a year, after the paid sick leave is exhausted, and is reimbursed by SSS; benefits under the SSS law are exempt from withholding (RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(B)(1)(e)). Customer input: the benefit SSS computes (the average daily salary credit needs contributions older than the 12 months the payroll history holds).

name: SSS maternity benefit (advanced)
description: The entry quantity is the SSS-computed maternity benefit advanced by the employer.

references.title: RA 11199 s.14-A as amended by RA 11210 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/86333, read 2026-10-07): a member with at least three monthly contributions in the twelve months before the semester of the contingency is paid 100% of her average daily salary credit, advanced in full by the employer within thirty days of the application and reimbursed by SSS; s.8(n)–(p): the average daily salary credit is the six highest monthly salary credits of those twelve months ÷ 180, the semester the two quarters ending in the quarter of the contingency. SSS Maternity Benefit page (https://www.sss.gov.ph/maternity-benefit/, read 2026-10-07): 105 days for a live birth, 120 for a solo parent, 60 for a miscarriage or emergency termination; "The computation of benefits under the Regular SSS Program shall be based on contributions up to 20,000 MSC." The contingency is `entry.occurred_on`, the event `entry.facts.event_kind` and the solo-parent claim `entry.facts.solo_parent_claimed`, as on the maternity leave; each month’s credit is its SSS base charged (`earned.history[].statutory.SSS.base`) on the contribution table’s ₱500 steps, ₱5,000 floor (₱1,000 for a kasambahay) and ₱20,000 Regular SS ceiling. The credits are this employer’s payroll only; contributions paid through an earlier employer count at SSS, so when this payroll holds fewer than three of the twelve months’ credits the class pays the entry amount — customer input: the benefit SSS computes (SSS also applies the three-contribution test there). Exempt from withholding as an SSS benefit (RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(B)(1)(e)).

name: Retirement benefit under a BIR-qualified plan (tax-exempt)
description: The entry quantity is the BIR-qualified plan benefit; the plan approval, age, service and once-only election gate the definition.

references.title: NIRC s.32(B)(6)(a) as amended by RA 4917 (https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1997/ra_8424_1997.html, read 2026-10-07): excluded from gross income are retirement benefits "received by officials and employees of private firms ... in accordance with a reasonable private benefit plan maintained by the employer: Provided, That the retiring official or employee has been in the service of the same employer for at least ten (10) years and is not less than fifty (50) years of age at the time of his retirement: Provided, further, That the benefits granted under this subparagraph shall be availed of by an official or employee only once". Gated on the entity fact `bir_qualified_retirement_plan` (the plan’s BIR approval), age fifty, 120 months’ service and the employee fact `retirement_plan_exemption_availed` (once in a lifetime); counts toward no tax base. Customer input: the plan benefit. Any other retirement payment is RETIREMENT_PAY_TAXABLE.
